text:
maya: quick heads-up, ran a targeted bake comparing FP8-KV vs INT8-KV with the new prefetch heuristic on the ivy30b shadow cluster. results are...interesting.
noah: can you paste the numbers? memory / p95 / p99?
maya: summary: INT8-KV reduces KV shard mem by ~38% on avg vs FP8-KV, but P95 token latency increased by ~15ms and we see P99 cold-start spikes (~120ms extra) on long-prefix traces.
srini: 38% mem is great. where is the spike coming from? dequant cost on the hot path?
maya: looks like a mix: dequant + extra cache miss penalties when prefetch policy misfires. i profiled a sample trace — dequant CPU time is ~6ms/step on the tracer host; cache-read fallback adds another 8-20ms depending on seq len.
adele: do you have the config you used? curious about batch sizes and prefetch window.
maya: config snippet:
```yaml
model: ivy30b
kv_quant: int8
prefetch:
  enabled: true
  window_tokens: 512
batching:
  max_batch_tokens: 2048
  timeout_ms: 12
```
maya: tests: 10k eval prompts (mix of chat/long-context). cold starts = first request after model idle>30s. warm = steady stream.
harry: what's the eval quality delta? any regen errors / hallucinations uptick?
maya: quality: perplexity +0.8% vs FP8-KV; exact-match on QA set down 0.6% absolute. not huge but above our regression alert threshold (0.5%).
noah: hmm. so memory savings vs small quality hit + latency tail. tradeoff depends on SLA. any run with hybrid (FP8 for primary KV, INT8 for tails)?
maya: we tried hybrid: primary shards FP8, cold-evicted shards INT8. hybrid gave 27% mem saving and P95 impact ~6ms (within SLA). quality deltas ~+0.2% perplexity (negligible).
srini: interesting. can you drop the raw perf table from the profiler? numbers per scenario.
maya: pasted raw CSV head:
```
scenario,mem_gb,p95_ms,p99_ms,perplexity,qa_em
fp8-kv,42.8,56,210,12.4,78.4
int8-kv,26.5,71,330,12.5,77.8
hybrid-kv,31.4,62,225,12.42,78.1
```
maya: note these are single-rep shadow runs. variance high on p99; need more runs for confidence.
adele: what's the plan? prefer hybrid for Dedicated? or add prefetch tuning first?
noah: my vote: conservative path = hybrid + small prefetch window (256) + canary on 10% traffic. that hits most wins without big regressions.
harry: ops note: if we can keep p99 under +50ms we can accept for dedicated non-enterprise tiers. enterprise needs stricter SLAs.
srini: action items:
- maya: kick 5 more shadow repeats for each scenario (fp8/int8/hybrid) and include p95/p99 CI (maya: due EOD)
- adele: run a small QA eval pass on the latest prompt set (automated) and report EM deltas (due EOD)
- noah: prepare canary rollout plan + policy stub for console (10% -> 50% if checks pass)
- deploybot: schedule a canary job template for dedicated-ivy30b pool
maya: filing follow-up ticket with raw traces + perf flamegraphs: LINK: https://redwood-internal/issue/ML-1422
noah: thanks. if hybrid holds up, we can default dedicated profiles to hybrid-kv and reserve int8-kv as an aggressive packing option.
adele: :thumbsup:
deploybot: scheduled canary job template created (job id cj-7731)
